extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, inventors, and legal professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of U.S. patent statutes and amendments (late 19th–early 20th century) specifying formalities, filing deadlines, substantive specification requirements, rights on death/insanity, design patent standards, caveats, issuance timing, penalties, remedies for government use, and related antitrust constraints affecting patent exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession of patent rights upon death or insanity (section 4896)
rubrics_metrics.description: "When any person, having made any new invention or discovery for which a patent might have been granted, dies before a patent is granted, the right of applying for and obtaining the patent shall devolve on his executor or administrator... in as full manner and on the same terms and conditions as the same might have been claimed or enjoyed by him in his lifetime; and when any person having made any new invention or discovery... becomes insane before a patent is granted, the right... shall devolve on his legally appointed guardian, conservator, or representative in trust for his estate..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers both death and insanity; legal representatives may make the application and the required oath or affirmation "shall be so varied in form that it can be made by them." The statutory language was amended to specify that the insane-person provision covers applications already on file or thereafter made. Also provides that foreign executors/administrators (where inventor was not domiciled in the U.S.) may apply if their authority is proved by certificate of a U.S. diplomatic or consular officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent issuance formality: seal and signature (section 4883)
rubrics_metrics.description: "All patents shall be issued in the name of the United States of America, under the seal of the Patent Office, and shall be signed by the Commissioner of Patents, and they shall be recorded, together with the specifications, in the Patent Office, in books to be kept for that purpose."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formal issuance requirements: title (U.S. of A.), seal, Commissioner's signature, and recording together with specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent novelty and statutory bars (section 4929)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Any person who has invented any new, original, and ornamental design for an article of manufacture, not known or used by others in this country before his invention thereof, and not patented or described in any printed publication in this or any foreign country before his invention thereof, or more than two years prior to his application, and not in public use or on sale in this country for more than two years prior to his application, unless the same is proved to have been abandoned, may... obtain a patent therefor."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets criteria for design patents: novelty, originality, ornamentality, not previously patented or printed public prior to invention (or more than two years prior to application), and not in public use or on sale in U.S. for more than two years before application unless abandoned. Requires payment of statutory fees and other proceedings analogous to utility inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority and novelty bars; Paris-term changes (section 4887)
rubrics_metrics.description: "An application... filed in this country by any person who has previously regularly filed an application for a patent for the same invention, discovery, or design in the foreign country... shall have the same force and effect... if the application in this country is filed within twelve months... and four months in cases of designs... from the earliest date on which any such foreign application was filed. But no patent shall be granted on an application... which had been patented or described in a printed publication... more than two years before the date of the actual filing of the application in this country, or which had been in public use, or on sale in this country for more than two years prior to such filing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes foreign priority/Paris Convention-style term (12 months for inventions, 4 months for designs) and reiterates the two-year statutory bar for prior patenting/printed publication/public use or sale in the U.S. before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant oath and authorized administrators (section 4892)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The applicant shall make oath that he does verily believe himself to be the original and first inventor or discoverer... that he does not know and does not believe that the same was ever before known or used; and shall state of what country he is a citizen. Such oath may be made before any person within the United States authorized by law to administer oaths, or, when the applicant resides in a foreign country, before any minister, charged'affaires, consul, or commercial agent... or before any notary public, judge, or magistrate having an official seal and authorized to administer oaths in the foreign country... whose authority shall be proved by certificate of a diplomatic or consular officer of the United States."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies both the content of the inventor's oath (originality/first inventor belief and citizenship) and the officials before whom the oath may be made domestically or abroad; requires proof of foreign official's authority by U.S. diplomatic/consular certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing and protection (section 4902)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Any person who makes any new invention or discovery and desires further time to mature the same may... file in the Patent Office a caveat setting forth the design thereof and of its distinguishing characteristics and praying protection of his right until he shall have matured his invention. Such caveat shall be filed in the confidential archives of the office and preserved in secrecy, and shall be operative for the term of one year... if application is made within the year by any other person for a patent with which such caveat would in any manner interfere, the Commissioner shall deposit the description, specification, drawings, and model of such application in like manner... and give notice thereof by mail to the person by whom the caveat was filed. If such person desires to avail himself of his caveat he shall file his descriptions, specifications, drawings, and model within three months from the time of placing the notice in the post-office in Washington..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a one-year confidential placeholder (caveat) that preserves a right to be notified of interfering applications; imposes timelines for the caveator to convert to a full application after notice (three months plus mailing allowance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent issuance and final fee timing (section 4885)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every patent shall issue within a period of three months from the date of the payment of the final fee, which fee shall be paid not later than six months from the time at which the application was passed and allowed and notice thereof was sent to the applicant or his agent; and if the final fee is not paid within that period the patent shall be withheld."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets deadlines for paying the final issue fee (within six months of allowance) and obligates the Patent Office to issue the patent within three months of payment; failure to pay within the permissible period results in withholding of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification, description, and claim requirements (R.S. §4888, as amended 1915)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Before any inventor or discoverer shall receive a patent... he shall file in the Patent Office a written description of the same, and of the manner and process of making, constructing, compounding, and using it, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art or science... to make, construct, compound, and use the same; and in case of a machine, he shall explain the principle thereof, and the best mode in which he has contemplated applying that principle, so as to distinguish it from other inventions; and he shall particularly point out and distinctly claim the part, improvement, or combination which he claims as his invention or discovery. The specification and claim shall be signed by the inventor."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies enablement, best mode (for machines), and requirement to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention; signature by inventor required. These are substantive patentability/formal requisites used to evaluate sufficiency of an application/specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for drawings when requisite (R.S. §4889, as amended 1915)
rubrics_metrics.description: "When the nature of the case admits of drawings, the applicant shall furnish one copy signed by the inventor or his attorney in fact, which shall be filed in the Patent Office; and a copy of the drawing to be furnished by the Patent Office, shall be attached to the patent as a part of the specification."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires filing of drawings when the subject matter admits of them; signed copy to be filed and a copy to be attached to the issued patent as part of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalties for forging or falsely altering letters patent (Section 27, March 4, 1909)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Whoever shall falsely make, forge, counterfeit, or alter any letters patent... or whoever shall pass, utter or publish as genuine any such forged, counterfeited, or falsely altered letters patent, knowing the same to be forged... shall be fined not more than five thousand dollars and imprisoned not more than ten years."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes criminal sanctions (fine and imprisonment) for forgery, counterfeiting, or false alteration and knowingly passing such forged patents as genuine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for patent owners against government use; limitations (Court of Claims Act, June 25, 1910)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Whenever an invention described in and covered by a patent of the United States shall hereafter be used by the United States without license of the owner... such owner may recover reasonable compensation for such use by suit in the Court of Claims: Provided, however, That said Court of Claims shall not entertain a suit... where the claim for compensation is based on the use by the United States of any article heretofore owned, leased, used by, or in the possession of the United States: Provided further, That... the benefits of this Act shall not inure to any patentee who, when he makes such claim is in the employment or service of the Government... nor shall this Act apply to any device discovered or invented by such employee during the time of his employment or service."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a right to recover reasonable compensation for uncompensated government use, but excludes claims where the U.S. already owned/used the article, permits government defenses available in infringement actions, and excludes patentees who are government employees (and their assignees) and inventions made during employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Assistant Commissioners (1914 amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Assistant Commissioner of Patents and the Assistant Commissioner of Patents shall hereafter perform such duties pertaining to the office of Commissioner of Patents as may be assigned to them, respectively, from time to time, by the Commissioner of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative delegation provision: Assistant Commissioners may be assigned duties by the Commissioner; relevant to internal office procedure and assignment of responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust prohibition: unlawful price discrimination (Antitrust Act §2)
rubrics_metrics.description: "It shall be unlawful for any person engaged in commerce... either directly or indirectly, to discriminate in price between different purchasers of commodities... where the effect of such discrimination may be to substantially lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits discriminatory pricing in commerce when its effect may substantially lessen competition or create monopoly, but exempts price differences honest due to differences in grade, quality, quantity, transportation costs, or price changes made in good faith to meet competition; sellers may select customers in bona fide transactions not in restraint of trade. Relevant to licensing/pricing of patented goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust prohibition: tying/conditional sales (Antitrust Act §3)
rubrics_metrics.description: "It shall be unlawful for any person engaged in commerce... to lease or make a sale or contract for sale of goods... whether patented or unpatented... on the condition, agreement or understanding that the lessee or purchaser thereof shall not use or deal in the goods... of a competitor... where the effect of such... condition... may be to substantially lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits conditioning sales or leases (including of patented articles) on agreements the buyer not use competitors' products when the effect may harm competition or tend toward monopoly (tying/restraints on resale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust private remedy: treble damages and venue (Antitrust Act §4)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Any person who shall be injured in his business or property by reason of anything forbidden in the antitrust laws may sue... and shall recover threefold the damages by him sustained, and the cost of suit, including a reasonable attorney's fee."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a private cause of action with treble damages and attorneys' fees for antitrust injuries; actions may be brought in district courts where defendant resides or is found or has an agent, without regard to amount in controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust administrative enforcement and proceedings (Antitrust Act §11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to enforce compliance with sections 2, 3, 7, and 8 is vested in the Interstate Commerce Commission for common carriers, the Federal Reserve Board for banks, and the Federal Trade Commission for other commerce. When such a commission/board has reason to believe a person is violating provisions, it shall issue a complaint, fix a hearing at least thirty days after service, allow intervention, reduce testimony to writing, and may issue cease-and-desist orders and require divestiture where appropriate. Enforcement may be sought in the circuit courts of appeals; findings supported by testimony are conclusive. Proceedings shall be expedited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the administrative enforcement process (complaint, notice, hearing, written record, orders to cease and desist and divestiture), rights to intervene, and subsequent judicial review/enforcement in courts of appeals with conclusive factual findings if supported by testimony. Important for patent holders/licensors insofar as licensing practices might invoke administrative antitrust action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust judgments and tolling of limitations (Antitrust Act §5 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: A final judgment or decree in any criminal prosecution or suit brought by or on behalf of the United States under the antitrust laws that a defendant has violated such laws shall be prima facie evidence against such defendant in any other suit under said laws; whenever any suit or proceeding is instituted by the United States to prevent, restrain, or punish violations of any of the antitrust laws the running of the statute of limitations in respect of each and every private right of action arising under said laws... shall be suspended during the pendency thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides evidentiary effect to governmental judgments and suspends statute of limitations for related private antitrust claims during pendency of government actions; affects timing and evidentiary strategy in antitrust litigation tied to patent licensing or conduct.
